_purpose: Every bespoke surface that diverges from docs/standards/ui-control-standards.md declares it HERE, clause by clause. Read by scripts/verify-ui-standard-divergence.mjs, which derives the clause list from the standard itself — so ADDING A CLAUSE TO THE STANDARD INVALIDATES EVERY DECLARATION UNTIL IT IS RE-ANSWERED. That is the order of operations (doc first, widget once, surfaces inherit) made mechanical.
_verdicts: met = the surface satisfies the clause. dropped = deliberately not taken, REQUIRES a reason. owed = a real gap, not yet closed, recorded rather than hidden. 'owed' is an honest answer and is meant to be used.
_rule: A declaration is not a waiver. 'dropped' with a sentence is a decision; 'owed' is a debt with a name. Neither is a pass.

baseline._note: BASELINE-AND-RATCHET, ruled by David 2026-09-03. A day-one hard fail would have been paid off with ~23 rubber-stamp declarations, and a declaration file full of rubber stamps is R-33's exact defect — a check incapable of disagreeing. These numbers may only SHRINK. When one drops, re-measure and commit the lower number.
baseline._undeclared_measured: 2026-09-03: 24 bespoke record-list surfaces under packages/cultivar-os/src, of which 1 (ReceiptsList) is declared. The other 23 are UNAUDITED — they have not been found wanting, they have not been looked at. Do not read this number as 23 known-good surfaces.
baseline._board_measured: 2026-09-03: ui-standards.html renders 3 of the 6 sections of the standard. Absent: G9, F4, E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, S1, R1, R2. E1 — 'one record, one edit surface' — is the clause that answers modal-vs-route, and it is not on the board a prompt-writer would check. Fixing the renderer drops this to 0.

divergences.shape_taken: SUMMARY ROW + INLINE DETAIL (record list with disclosure) — one card per receipt, the receipt → order → delivery chain nested inside it.
divergences.reason: Each row carries a variable-length chain (0..n orders, each with 0..n deliveries). A fixed-column grid can render that only by truncating the chain or by exploding one receipt into several rows — and a receipt appearing twice because it has two orders is precisely the confusion this screen exists to remove. Two LAWNS receipts are duplicate captures of one invoice; making them look like four rows would defeat the surface.
divergences.recorded_where: ReceiptsList.tsx header (UI STANDARD block) · this declaration · docs/decisions/2026-09-03-ui-standard-divergence-report.md · CLOSE-OUT-LEDGER #264. NOT on ui-standards.html — the board renders no per-surface rows at all yet, which is the reader gap tracked as baseline.clauses_absent_from_board.
divergences.note: 🔴 THIS IS THE DECLARATION THAT PROVES THE CAP. The original divergence was REASONED AND CORRECT about the shape, and still defective: it explained dropping the grid and said NOTHING about G4, G5 and G6, which the surface also does not have. The narrow record read as a complete one. Answering all nine clauses is what surfaces that.

G1.reason: There is no header row to make sticky — the shape is a card list, not a table. The need G1 serves (never lose which column you are reading) does not arise when every value is labelled in place on its own card.

G2.reason: There is no horizontal axis: cards wrap within the page width, so there is no h-scrollbar to make reachable.

G3.reason: No columns, so no identifier column to freeze. The vendor name is the first thing on every card and never scrolls away from its own row.

G4.reason: 🔴 A REAL GAP, AND IT IS ONE OF THE THREE THE ORIGINAL DIVERGENCE NOTE WAS SILENT ABOUT. There is no sort control of any kind — the order is fixed by G9 and the owner cannot re-sort by vendor, amount or category. Defensible at 17 rows; it is not defensible as an unrecorded omission.

G5.reason: There are no columns to show or hide. The card shows a fixed set of six facts and the operator cannot trim it — which is a consequence of the shape, not an independent decision. If the card grows past what fits on one screen this becomes owed rather than dropped.

G6.reason: 🔴 A REAL GAP, THE SECOND OF THE THREE. No text search and no status filter, on a surface whose own count label admits it caps at 100. At 17 rows an owner reads the screen; at 100 they cannot, and the cap says 100 is expected.

G7.reason: 🔴 THE THIRD. The cards are not in a bounded scroll box — they scroll the page — and there is no compact density. The standard's own reason applies directly: G7 exists because a list is expected to hold hundreds. The build's header addressed only VIRTUALISATION ('nothing here that needs virtualising at 17 rows'), which is a different clause of G7 and is a fair call; the density and bounded-box half was never answered.

G8.reason: The surface is READ-ONLY by ruling — it issues one .select() and writes nothing. Editing a receipt lives at /receipts/:id (ReceiptDetail), which is the record's ONE edit surface under E1. Adding inline edit here would create the second editor E1 forbids.

G9.reason: Ordered by receipts.date — the date on the document — with created_at as tiebreak only. Asserted in the model by compareReceiptsForDisplay and probed by E7, which is constructed so the two candidate orders DISAGREE on its inputs (the previous probe varied created_at alone and would have passed either way).
